hosting.//rewrites: Still no catch-all to /404.html. A Hosting rewrite preserves the URL and returns 200, so every nonexistent path would serve the 404 page as a success and get indexed as duplicate content. With no rewrite, Hosting serves out/404.html with a real 404 status — which is what src/app/not-found.tsx emits it for. The /events/** entry below is the ONE deliberate exception and is scoped to that prefix for exactly that reason. It works because Hosting resolves in a fixed order — redirects, then exact static files, then rewrites — so /events and /events/some-liturgy are served from disk and never reach it; only a path with no file falls through. Order matters within this array too: it is first-match, so the three /api entries must stay ABOVE the glob or checkout would render a gallery shell. /api/bulletin is the homepage schedule's live read: it follows config/active_bulletin in the announcements project, because the section is baked into static HTML at build time and would otherwise never change until a redeploy.

rewrites.//forms: The forms endpoint. `submit` is what every parish form posts to — it validates against the stored definition, prices the answers server-side, takes the Square payment, and pushes a vehicle registration into the Taksis project. It stays ABOVE the /forms/** glob below, for the first-match reason the note at the top of this array gives for the /api entries. Two Breeze endpoints sat here until 2026-09-01 and went with the Breeze importer.

rewrites.//forms-upload: Issues a signed URL for one photograph attached to a form, and is the ONLY way bytes reach formUploads/ now: storage.rules refuses every client create there. It replaced an anonymous `allow create: if isImage()` rule whose only real wall was App Check enforcement on the Storage service — which had to come off on 2026-09-03 because it also refused every on the public site. This endpoint verifies an App Check token in its own code, so that setting does not reach it. Above the /forms/** glob below for the same first-match reason as the entries around it.

rewrites.//camp: A servant signing themselves up. Unauthenticated like /api/forms/submit, and above the /forms/** glob for the same first-match reason — the page it is posted from is /forms/summer-camp.

rewrites.//account: A servant deleting their own account. Authenticated — it acts on whoever the verified ID token says is calling and takes no uid from the request body, so there is no version of this endpoint that deletes somebody else. Above the /forms/** glob for the same first-match reason as the two entries before it.

rewrites.//finance: Recomputing the camp and form money on demand. Not under /api/square — none of it goes near Square. Writes, so it is guarded by the same grant that reads the documents it writes; see functions/src/finance.ts.

rewrites.//calendar: The church schedule. It cannot be read from the page: Breeze puts its event data behind a session cookie its own embed page sets, on its own origin, with no CORS header. It also cannot be baked at build time — a "this week" view baked into static HTML is whatever week the deploy ran in. The `scope=servants` variant needs a verified `servant` claim and is the whole of what used to be the /servants page.

rewrites.//gallery-upload: Issues a signed URL for one gallery photograph, and writes the galleryMedia document that goes with it. It is the ONLY way either now happens: storage.rules refuses every client write to submissions/ and firestore.rules refuses every client create of galleryMedia, so a browser cannot reach the bucket or the collection on its own. That is deliberate — the old path uploaded bytes first and wrote the document second, so a script that skipped the second step skipped every check the project had and left objects in a billed bucket that never appeared in the review queue. This endpoint verifies an App Check token, counts the upload against a daily quota, and never sees a byte of the photograph. It MUST stay above the /events/** glob below: rewrites are first-match, and beneath it this address would serve a gallery shell instead of running.

rewrites.//forms-shell: The second deliberate exception to the no-catch-all rule, and it works for exactly the reason the /events/** entry above does: Hosting resolves redirects, then exact static files, then rewrites, so /forms is served from out/forms.html and never reaches this line — only /forms/<slug>, which has no file, falls through. That is the point. Individual forms are deliberately not exported: staff publish one from the drawer on /forms and it is reachable immediately, with no deploy and nobody with deploy rights involved. The shell reads the slug from the address bar. robots.ts disallows /forms/ so the 200 this returns is never indexed as duplicate content.

hosting.//redirects: REMOVED: /calendar -> /events. It was written when /calendar was only a Wix URL, and then this site grew a real /calendar page. Hosting evaluates redirects BEFORE it looks for static files, so the redirect won and the Calendar link in the main nav 301'd away from the page it points at — in production only, because `next dev` knows nothing about this file. Anything added here from now on must be checked against apps/website/src/app for a route of the same name. Every URL below is one the Wix site published, taken from its sitemap while it was still up — after the cutover that list is unrecoverable. 301 rather than 302: these moves are permanent, and a 302 tells search engines to keep indexing the old URL. The source paths are Wix template names nobody chose, which is the whole reason for this table: /projects-7-2 is the ministry that feeds the homeless, and no one could read, guess, or say that out loud. Titles lie, so each destination was checked by loading the page: /team-3 is titled 'Calendar & Events' and is the activities page, NOT the clergy page it sounds like — the clergy bios are on /who-we-are. Mapping notes: /lesson-* are catechism pages (Intro, Young Christ, Saint Mina) but all three are empty Wix templates with no content; they land on /welcome because that is where a newcomer following an old link should end up, not because there is anything to preserve. Wix filed ministries and past events alike under `projects` — /projects-7-1, -7-2, -7-3 are the ongoing College & Young Professionals, Mother of Mercy, and St. Simon for Seniors ministries and now land on their own named anchors under /ministries; /projects-7, -7-4, -8 are the 2024 and 2023 festivals and Summer Camp 2024, which have already happened, so the calendar is the honest destination rather than a page invented for them. /portfolio already 404s on Wix and is redirected anyway, because it costs one line. The last entry is not a Wix URL: /clergy was a page on this site until the biographies moved into the homepage as disclosures, and anyone who typed it, bookmarked it, or linked it during development should land on the section rather than on a 404.

redirects.//servants: Both of these used to be pages. The servants schedule is no longer its own screen — it appears inside /calendar for whoever signs in with a church account — so the Wix URL and the one this site published both land there. Checked against apps/website/src/app: there is no /servants route any more, which is what makes a redirect safe here. See the note above the redirects array.

hosting.//headers: Cache headers for /service-worker.js and /manifest.webmanifest were removed: neither file exists yet, and there is no apps/website/public/ at all. Restore them in the same commit that adds the real PWA files.

headers.//: The flythrough on /about/future-plans, and its cue track. 33 MB, and it AUTOPLAYS — so without this every visit to that page refetches it under Hosting's one-hour default, and the page is linked from the About menu on every page of the site. A day of caching with a week of stale-while-revalidate: long enough that a reader who comes back tomorrow pays nothing, short enough that a re-cut of the film reaches everybody within a day. NOT `immutable`, unlike the /_next/static rule above — those filenames carry a content hash and these do not, so the file at this path can genuinely change.

The security headers, on every response Hosting serves — pages, assets, and the /api/** rewrites onto Cloud Functions alike. Hosting applies the first matching `source` per header name, so this glob sits BELOW the /_next/static/** cache entry and never competes with it: they set different header names.
headers.//csp: Content-Security-Policy, and the two things worth knowing before editing it. (1) `script-src` carries 'unsafe-inline' and cannot not carry it. A nonce has to be minted per response by a server, and Decision #6 says there is no server — the site is a static export and Next hydrates through inline <script> blocks that are part of every exported page. What this still buys is the host allowlist: an injected <script src="https://somewhere-else"> does not load, which is the shape most third-party compromises actually take. (2) `img-src` is deliberately open to https:. An image cannot execute, and a book added in Square today gets a cover URL on a Square-owned host we have never seen — a tight list there would silently blank new covers, which is exactly the sort of failure that gets a whole CSP deleted six months later. Every other directive is an explicit list and should stay one. The named hosts, so a removal is a decision rather than a tidy-up: gstatic and www.google.com are reCAPTCHA Enterprise, which is App Check; squarecdn is the Web Payments SDK loader, js.squareup.com is where the Apple Pay and Google Pay buttons come from, and pci-connect.squareup.com is where a card is tokenised — all three are named twice because Square's sandbox is a different host rather than a different path, and a policy that only knew production would fail in dev in a way nobody would connect to this file; maps.google.com is the map on /contact; youtube is the player on /livestream; give.tithe.ly is the giving form we frame ourselves rather than let give.js open a tab; spsm-database.firebaseapp.com is the hidden iframe Firebase Auth signs Microsoft accounts in through, and removing it breaks every sign-in. apis.google.com is the loader that *builds* that iframe — `signInWithPopup` fetches https://apis.google.com/js/api.js before it opens anything, so with the host missing from `script-src` the popup never opens at all and the SDK reports the block as `auth/internal-error`, which names nothing. Both hosts are needed; one without the other is still a broken sign-in.
headers.//csp-connect: www.google.com and www.gstatic.com are in `connect-src` as well as `script-src`, and that pair is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces. reCAPTCHA Enterprise does not finish its work in the script it loads: it POSTs the assessment to https://www.google.com/recaptcha/enterprise/clr with `fetch`, which `connect-src` governs and `script-src` does not. Without them the script loads, the request is refused by the policy, App Check never mints a token, and because App Check enforcement is ON for Firestore and Storage, EVERY browser read of either comes back `permission-denied` — the forms list falls back to its two built-ins, /events sits on "Loading…" forever, and a signed-in servant has no grants. None of that reproduces locally: `lib/firebase.ts` uses the App Check DEBUG TOKEN on localhost, which is a bypass, so the reCAPTCHA exchange never happens on a laptop. This was the whole of "production does not work anything like local" on 2026-09-02. Note the reCAPTCHA key ALSO has its own domain allowlist, which is separate from this file and has to contain whatever host the site is served from.
headers.//frame-ancestors: frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options DENY say the same thing twice, on purpose — the second is for anything old enough not to read the first. Nothing may frame this site. If the parish ever wants a page of it embedded somewhere (the Wix site at www.spsmwayland.org is the only plausible candidate), both of these have to change together, and 'self' is not enough — it must name that origin.
headers.//hsts: A year, without includeSubDomains or preload, and that restraint is the point. Hosting already serves HSTS on its own domains; this is what follows the site onto a custom domain. includeSubDomains would bind every subdomain of spsmwayland.org to HTTPS the moment one visitor loaded this site — including any the parish still runs elsewhere, which would go dark with no way to reach them and no way to take it back inside a year.
headers.//coop: same-origin-allow-popups, not same-origin. Sign-in is a Microsoft popup opened by the Firebase SDK, and it has to be able to talk back to the window that opened it; same-origin severs that and the popup closes having signed nobody in.

functions.//predeploy: Rebuilds @spsm/shared and then the bundle. Without this a deploy can ship a lib/ built against an older shared package, which typechecks locally and fails at runtime in a way nothing catches.
functions.//ignore: .secret.local holds dummy values for the emulator and has no business in a deployed artifact. dist/ is the intermediate tsc output; only the bundled lib/ is needed.
